#### Homogeneity 4: Identical and independent attachment 

In a [bipartite random network NPSEM](#def-bipartite-npsem-ie), each row of the adjacency matrix ${\Psi}_{si}$ (person $i$'s network weights) belongs to person $i$'s observational unit. Identical structural distributions then say that every row is generated by the same $1 \times q$ array of equations $F_{{\mathbf \Psi_s}}$, and single-world independence says that the rows are independent; in particular, $\mathbf U_{{\Psi}_{si}}$, the rows of the $p \times q$ matrix of error terms $\mathbf U_{{\Psi}_{s}}$, are independent. Each person in the model attaches to a selection of places independently of any other person and based on identical equations. This is not an extra assumption of the [BRNFFRCISTG](#def-brnffrcistg); it is what the model's assumptions say about the rows. 

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Structural: Places } (\mathbb{R}) \\
&   R_{sj}                   & &= f_{ R_s}( U_{ R_{sj}},   g_{VR}(\mathbf{V}_{s-1}, {[\mathbf \Psi^T_s]}_{j}) ) \\
&   T_{sj}                   & &= f_{ T_s}( U_{ T_{sj}},  R_{sj})                                 \\
\text{Structural: People } (\mathbb{R}) \\
&   M_{si}                  & &=     f_{ M_s} ( U_{ M_{si}} ,  V_{s-1,i},    M_{s-1, i},  g_{TM}(\mathbf{T}_{s}, {\Psi}_{si}))       \\
&   V_{si}                  & &=     f_{ V_s}( U_{ V_{si}},  M_{si},  V_{s-1, i})                                                \\
\text{Structural: People in places } (\mathbb{R}^{1 \times q}) \\
&  {\Psi}_{si}   & &= F_{{\mathbf \Psi_s}}(\mathbf U_{{\Psi}_{si}}, \mathbf{V}_{s-1}, \mathbf{\Psi}_{s-1})  \\
\end{aligned}
$$




where ${[\mathbf \Psi^T_s]}_{j}$ is the $j^{th}$ row of the transpose of the adjacency matrix $\mathbf{\Psi}_{s}$ and 

$$
\mathbf U_{{\Psi}_{si}} \perp \mathbf U_{{\Psi}_{sj}} \text{ for } i \neq j
$$
